author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of the diverse motions of Nature and of Grace

verses.text: “My Son, pay diligent heed to the motions of Nature and of Grace, because they move in a very contrary and subtle manner, and are hardly distinguished save by a spiritual and inwardly enlightened man.
verses.modernizedText: “My Son, pay careful attention to the movements of Nature and Grace, because they move in very different and subtle ways and are hardly distinguished except by a spiritual and inwardly enlightened person.

verses.text: All men indeed seek good, and make pretence of something good in all that they say or do; and thus under the appearance of good many are deceived.
verses.modernizedText: All people indeed seek good and make a pretense of something good in all they say or do; thus many are deceived under the appearance of good.

verses.text: “Nature is deceitful and draweth away, ensnareth, and deceiveth many, and always hath self for her end; but Grace walketh in simplicity and turneth away from every appearance of evil, maketh no false pretences, and doeth all entirely for the sake of God, in whom also she finally resteth.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature is deceitful and draws away, ensnares, and deceives many, and always has herself as her end; but Grace walks in simplicity and turns away from every appearance of evil, makes no false pretense, and does everything entirely for God’s sake, in whom she also finally rests.

verses.text: “Nature is very unwilling to die, and to be pressed down, and to be overcome, and to be in subjection, and to bear the yoke readily; but Grace studieth self-mortification, resisteth sensuality, seeketh to be subdued, longeth to be conquered, and willeth not to use her own liberty.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature is very unwilling to die, to be pressed down and overcome, to be in subjection, and readily to bear the yoke; but Grace studies self-mortification, resists sensuality, seeks to be subdued, longs to be conquered, and does not wish to use her own liberty.

verses.text: She loveth to be held by discipline, and not to have authority over any, but always to live, to remain, to have her being under God, and for God’s sake is ready to be humbly subject to every ordinance of man.
verses.modernizedText: She loves to be held by discipline and not to have authority over anyone, but always to live, remain, and have her being under God, and for God’s sake is ready to be humbly subject to every ordinance of man.

verses.text: “Nature laboureth for her own advantage, and considereth what profit she may gain from another; but Grace considereth more, not what may be useful and convenient to self, but what may be profitable to the many.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature labors for her own advantage and considers what profit she may gain from another; but Grace considers more, not what may be useful and convenient to herself, but what may profit the many.

verses.text: “Nature willingly receiveth honour and reverence; but Grace faithfully ascribeth all honour and glory to God.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature willingly receives honor and reverence; but Grace faithfully ascribes all honor and glory to God.

verses.text: “Nature feareth confusion and contempt, but Grace rejoiceth to suffer shame for the name of Jesus.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature fears confusion and contempt, but Grace rejoices to suffer shame for the name of Jesus.

verses.text: “Nature loveth ease and bodily quiet; Grace cannot be unemployed, but gladly embraceth labour.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature loves ease and bodily quiet; Grace cannot remain idle, but gladly embraces labor.

verses.text: “Nature seeketh to possess things curious and attractive, and abhorreth those which are rough and cheap; Grace is delighted with things simple and humble, despiseth not those which are rough, nor refuseth to be clothed with old garments.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature seeks to possess curious and attractive things and hates those that are rough and cheap; Grace delights in things simple and humble, does not despise rough things, or refuse to be clothed in old garments.

verses.text: “Nature hath regard to things temporal, rejoiceth in earthly lucre, is made sad by loss, vexed by any little injurious word; but Grace reacheth after things eternal, cleaveth not to those which are temporal, is not perturbed by losses, nor embittered by any hard words, because she hath placed her treasure and joy in heaven where nought perisheth.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature regards temporal things, rejoices in earthly gain, is saddened by loss, and vexed by any little hurtful word; but Grace reaches for eternal things, does not cling to temporal things, and is neither disturbed by losses nor embittered by harsh words, because she has placed her treasure and joy in heaven, where nothing perishes.

verses.text: “Nature is covetous, and receiveth more willingly than she giveth, loveth things that are personal and private to herself; while Grace is kind and generous, avoideth selfishness, is contented with a little, believeth that it is more blessed to give than to receive.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature is covetous and receives more willingly than she gives; she loves things that are personal and private to herself; while Grace is kind and generous, avoids selfishness, is content with a little, and believes that it is more blessed to give than to receive.

verses.text: “Nature inclineth thee to created things, to thine own flesh, to vanities and dissipation; but Grace draweth to God and to virtues, renounceth creatures, fleeth from the world, hateth the desires of the flesh, restraineth vagaries, blusheth to be seen in public.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature inclines you toward created things, your own flesh, vanities, and dissipation; but Grace draws you toward God and virtues, renounces creatures, flees from the world, hates the desires of the flesh, restrains wandering impulses, and blushes to be seen in public.

verses.text: “Nature is glad to receive some outward solace in which the senses may have delight; but Grace seeketh to be comforted in God alone, and to have delight in the chief good above all visible things.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature is glad to receive some outward comfort in which the senses may delight; but Grace seeks to be comforted in God alone and to delight in the chief good above all visible things.

verses.text: “Nature doeth everything for her own gain and profit, can do nothing as a free favour, but hopeth to attain something as good or better, or some praise or favour for her benefits; and she loveth that her own deeds and gifts should be highly valued; but Grace seeketh nothing temporal, nor requireth any other gift of reward than God alone; neither longeth she for more of temporal necessities than such as may suffice for the attaining of eternal life.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature does everything for her own gain and profit, can do nothing as a free favor, but hopes to obtain something as good or better, or some praise or favor for her benefits; and she loves to have her deeds and gifts highly valued. But Grace seeks nothing temporal and requires no other gift of reward than God alone; nor does she long for more temporal necessities than may suffice to attain eternal life.

verses.text: “Nature rejoiceth in many friends and kinsfolk, she boasteth of noble place and noble birth, she smileth on the powerful, flattereth the rich, applaudeth those who are like herself; but Grace loveth even her enemies, and is not lifted up by the multitude of friends, setteth no store upon high place or high birth, unless there be greater virtue therewith; favoureth the poor man more than the rich, hath more sympathy with the innocent than with the powerful; rejoiceth with the truthful, not with the liar; always exhorteth the good to strive after better gifts of grace, and to become by holiness like unto the Son of God.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature rejoices in many friends and relatives, boasts of high position and noble birth, smiles on the powerful, flatters the rich, and applauds those like herself; but Grace loves even her enemies and is not lifted up by a multitude of friends. She sets no store by high position or birth unless greater virtue accompanies them, favors the poor more than the rich, sympathizes more with the innocent than the powerful, rejoices with the truthful rather than the liar, and always urges the good to strive after better gifts of grace and to become like the Son of God through holiness.

verses.text: “Nature quickly complaineth of poverty and of trouble; Grace beareth want with constancy.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature quickly complains of poverty and trouble; Grace bears want with constancy.

verses.text: “Nature looketh upon all things in reference to herself; striveth and argueth for self; but Grace bringeth back all things to God from whom they came at the beginning; ascribeth no good to herself nor arrogantly presumeth; is not contentious, nor preferreth her own opinion to others, but in every sense and understanding submitteth herself to the Eternal wisdom and the Divine judgment.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature looks at all things in relation to herself and strives and argues for herself; but Grace brings all things back to God, from whom they came in the beginning. She ascribes no good to herself, is not arrogantly presumptuous or contentious, and does not prefer her own opinion to others, but in every sense and understanding submits herself to Eternal wisdom and Divine judgment.

verses.text: “Nature is eager to know secrets and to hear new things; she loveth to appear abroad, and to make experience of many things through the senses; she desireth to be acknowledged and to do those things which win praise and admiration; but Grace careth not to gather up new or curious things, because all this springeth from the old corruption, whereas there is nothing new or lasting upon earth.
verses.modernizedText: “Nature is eager to know secrets and hear new things; she loves to appear in public and experience many things through the senses; she desires recognition and to do things that win praise and admiration. But Grace does not care to gather up new or curious things, because all this springs from the old corruption, whereas nothing on earth is new or lasting.

verses.text: So she teacheth to restrain the senses, to shun vain complacency and ostentation, to hide humbly those things which merit praise and real admiration, and from everything and in all knowledge to seek after useful fruit, and the praise and honour of God.
verses.modernizedText: So she teaches us to restrain the senses, to shun vain complacency and display, to hide humbly the things that merit praise and real admiration, and to seek useful fruit and the praise and honor of God from everything and in all knowledge.

verses.text: She desireth not to receive praise for herself or her own, but longeth that God be blessed in all His gifts, who out of unmingled love bestoweth all things.”
verses.modernizedText: She does not desire to receive praise for herself or her own, but longs that God, who out of pure love bestows all things, be blessed in all His gifts.”

verses.text: This Grace is a supernatural light, and a certain special gift of God, and the proper mark of the elect, and the pledge of eternal salvation; it exalteth a man from earthly things to love those that are heavenly; and it maketh the carnal man spiritual.
verses.modernizedText: This Grace is a supernatural light and a certain special gift of God, the proper mark of the elect and the pledge of eternal salvation; it raises a person from earthly things to love heavenly things and makes the carnal person spiritual.

verses.text: So far therefore as Nature is utterly pressed down and overcome, so far is greater Grace bestowed and the inner man is daily created anew by fresh visitations, after the image of God.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore, to the extent that Nature is utterly pressed down and overcome, greater Grace is bestowed, and the inner person is daily created anew by fresh visitations after the image of God.
